brute_force_nested.label: Nested Loops (Brute Force)
brute_force_nested.tier1: Notice how your inner loop scans elements repeatedly. What happens to previous pairs on each step?
brute_force_nested.tier2: Can you eliminate the nested scan with an auxiliary lookup structure like a hash map or frequency array to achieve O(n)?

hash_optimization.label: Hash Map / Key-Value Lookup
hash_optimization.tier1: You are querying an auxiliary map. Verify if you are checking the complement condition before or after storing the current key.
hash_optimization.tier2: Make sure you don't match an element with itself when indices are involved (e.g. `seen[complement] != i`).

pointer_convergence.label: Converging Two-Pointers
pointer_convergence.tier1: Your two pointers shrink the problem boundary. Check the exact while-loop condition (`left < right` vs `left <= right`).
pointer_convergence.tier2: Ensure each branch strictly moves at least one pointer forward; otherwise, identical duplicate values may cause an infinite loop.

stack_pattern.label: LIFO Stack Container
stack_pattern.tier1: You are pushing and popping elements. What occurs if a closing symbol arrives when the stack is completely empty?
stack_pattern.tier2: Remember to check whether the stack is empty after the iteration finishes (e.g., unmatched open brackets leftover).

binary_search.label: Binary Search Bisection
binary_search.tier1: You are halving the search window. Ensure your midpoint computation does not result in an off-by-one or infinite loop on 2-element ranges.
binary_search.tier2: Verify your pointer updates: `left = mid + 1` vs `right = mid - 1`. If you keep `left = mid`, integer division can freeze convergence.

single_pass.label: Single Pass Traversal
single_pass.tier1: You're scanning the input in a single pass. Verify what state variables need to be updated before the next element is processed.
single_pass.tier2: Consider whether maintaining a running maximum, running sum, or monotonic state would solve the query without multiple passes.

recursive.label: Recursive Traversal
recursive.tier1: Check your base case termination criteria. Does every branch reach a condition where no further recursive call is made?
recursive.tier2: Inspect call stack overhead and repeated subproblems. Would memoizing intermediate results prevent exponential branching?

linear_search_in_loop.label: Linear Search Inside Loop
linear_search_in_loop.tier1: You are doing an `x in collection` scan inside your loop. Searching a Python list takes O(n) time on every step.
linear_search_in_loop.tier2: Convert the list to a `set` or `dict` before entering the loop. Membership tests in sets operate in O(1) average time.

unknown.label: Algorithmic Invariant
unknown.tier1: Trace your code step-by-step with the simplest failing test case. Which variable diverges first from your expected mental model?
unknown.tier2: Formulate the algorithm's loop invariant: what condition must stay true before and after each iteration of your main loop?
